reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight emerges from treating each fraternity as a stochastic system governed by two competing causal forces—complete immunity and full disease manifestation. This leads to a bimodal outcome rather than a continuous normal distribution. The conditional inference primitive formalizes the likelihood of contagion within a fraternity given one known case. The double-hump distribution arises because the data does not conform to a single bell-shaped curve due to these two dominant modes. The failure mode lies in assuming homogeneity or continuity where there is a clear dichotomy in causal influence. The mathematical derivation shows that the probability of a second individual being consumptive depends on the observed prevalence within the fraternity, which itself reflects the underlying bimodal nature of transmission. Thus, the system exhibits non-Gaussian behavior that cannot be captured by standard statistical tools.
